Name: Chaos Room
Notes: One-room museum crammed with an overwhelming array of art and objects.

Name: Abandoned Western Village
Notes: Derelict Wild-West theme park full of decaying animatronic cowboys. Check access rules; don't trespass.

Name: Yokai Yashiki (Monster & Stone Museum)
Notes: Folk monsters of the Iya Valley plus the region's unique geology, at Michi-no-Eki Oboke.

Name: Ashizuri Underwater Observation Tower
Notes: Tower that lets you walk down below the waves to watch coral and fish.

Name: Dainichibo Temple (Sokushinbutsu)
Notes: Temple housing a self-mummified Buddhist monk.

Name: Ryusendo Cave
Notes: Limestone cave with some of the clearest underground lakes in the world.

Name: Okunoshima (Rabbit Island)
Notes: Island overrun by friendly rabbits; also a WWII poison-gas museum.

Name: Sogenji (Kappa-dera Temple)
Notes: Temple dedicated to the kappa, with a mummified kappa hand.

Name: Gunkanjima (Hashima Island)
Notes: Abandoned coal-mining island city; visit by boat tour.

Name: Akihabara Electric Town
Notes: Electronics, anime, manga and retro games.

Name: Yokai Street (Ichijo-dori)
Notes: Shopping street lined with handmade yokai figures.

Name: Sanrio Puroland
Notes: Indoor Hello Kitty theme park.

Name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
Notes: Snow monkeys bathing in hot springs (best in winter).

Name: Sagano (Arashiyama) Bamboo Forest
Notes: Towering bamboo grove; go at sunrise to beat the crowds.

Name: Little World Museum of Man
Notes: Open-air anthropology theme park with buildings and food from ~20 countries.

Name: Maishima Incineration Plant
Notes: Hundertwasser-designed waste plant that looks like a fairytale castle.

Name: Cup Noodles Museum Osaka Ikeda
Notes: Make your own Cup Noodle where instant ramen was invented.

Name: Miyoshi Mononoke Museum
Notes: Japan's yokai museum, built around the Inoue/Yumoto collection.

Name: Lake Imba Monster
Notes: Local legend of a monster in Lake Inba-numa.

Name: Funato Kappa Park
Notes: Homemade kappa statues, each with its own personality.

Name: Weird Museum for Boys and Girls
Notes: Kitsch pop-culture and Showa-era oddities museum.

Name: Hachijo Royal Hotel (abandoned)
Notes: Japan's largest abandoned hotel on remote Hachijo island. Exterior only.

Name: Tenshou-Kyousha Shrine Mermaid Mummy
Notes: Reportedly 1,400-year-old mermaid mummy.

Name: Henn-na Hotel
Notes: Hotel run by robots, incl. dinosaur receptionists.

Name: Atomic Bomb Medical Museum
Notes: Medical effects of the Nagasaki bombing (Nagasaki University).

Name: Museum of Tropical Medicine
Notes: Specimens and history of tropical diseases (Nagasaki University).

Name: Tobacco & Salt Museum
Notes: Cultural history of tobacco and salt, once state monopolies.

Name: Tamon-ji (Tanuki Temple)
Notes: Tanuki legend, a rare Edo-era wooden gate, survivor of the Tokyo bombings.

Name: Tomb of Jesus Christ
Notes: Village claiming to be Jesus's final resting place.

Name: Taiyo Park
Notes: Overgrown park full of replica world landmarks and stone figures.

Name: Kaiyodo Kappa Museum
Notes: Whimsical museum devoted to the cucumber-loving kappa.

Name: Hundred Caves of Yoshimi
Notes: Ancient hillside burial caves.

Name: Nima Sand Museum
Notes: Glass pyramids housing the world's largest hourglass, near singing-sand beach.

Name: Radium Onsen
Notes: Old bathhouse with an option to soak in (mildly) radioactive water.

Name: Mount Tanigawa
Notes: Beautiful but notoriously deadly mountain; take the ropeway for views.

Name: Doai Station
Notes: Japan's 'mole station', 462 steps underground.

Name: Hida Takayama Teddy Bear Eco Village
Notes: 1,000+ teddy bears dressed for every profession.

Name: Takayama Showa-kan Museum
Notes: 60 years of Showa pop culture, from Godzilla to Hulk Hogan.

Name: Nawate Dori (Frog Street)
Notes: Riverside street of frog statues, stalls and a frog shrine.

Name: Kappabashi Sampuru Shops
Notes: 'Kitchen Town' with shops selling realistic plastic food replicas.

Name: Tetsugakudo Park
Notes: Philosophy-themed park founded by an occult expert.

Name: Yokai Art Museum
Notes: Contemporary yokai art in old warehouses on Shodoshima.

Name: Green Thumb
Notes: Herbal teas, cosmetics and 'kitchen witch' dolls.

Name: Sanatorium – Wonder Museum Annex
Notes: Tuberculosis-sanatorium-themed cafe doubling as an underground gallery.

Name: Kenashi Pond (Seiryu Shrine)
Notes: Pond said to be haunted by a giant white snake.

Name: Kabosu the Doge Statue
Notes: Bronze statue of the shiba inu behind the 'Doge' meme (Sakura Furusato Hiroba).

Name: Tomb of the Nue
Notes: Tomb of a chimeric monster whose corpse washed ashore in Osaka.

Name: Ogushi Kaizuka Park
Notes: Shell-midden park with a giant statue of the clam-eating giant Daidarabotchi.

Name: Kiso Valley
Notes: Forested valley of Edo-era Nakasendo post towns (Narai, Kiso-Fukushima, Tsumago); stay in a traditional minshuku.

Name: Mount Asama
Notes: Active volcano on the Nagano–Gunma border; base yourself in Karuizawa or the Asama highlands.

Name: Toyone Village Hall
Notes: Tiny mountain village in the far north-east of Aichi.

Name: Shitara Village
Notes: Rural Okumikawa town in the Aichi mountains.

Name: Shirakawa-go
Notes: UNESCO village of thatched gassho-zukuri farmhouses; some take overnight guests.

Name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Atomic Bomb Dome)
Notes: A-Bomb Dome, Peace Memorial Park and Museum.

Name: Nagoya Castle
Notes: Golden shachihoko and the rebuilt Honmaru Palace.

Name: RAKU SPA GARDEN Nagoya
Notes: Large spa with natural hot spring and bedrock baths.

Name: Ishigaki Island
Notes: Kabira Bay, manta snorkelling, gateway to the Yaeyama islands.

Name: Immersive Journey Nagoya
Notes: Immersive digital-art/VR venue, Skyle 10F, Sakae (opened Jan 2026).

Name: Monet's Pond (Nemichi Shrine pond)
Notes: Clear spring pond with koi that looks like Monet's Water Lilies.

Name: Asakura Museum of Sculpture
Notes: Sculptor Asakura Fumio's house, studio and rooftop garden.

Name: Mount Osore (Osorezan Bodaiji)
Notes: Volcanic 'gateway to the underworld' temple. Open May–Oct.

Name: Maboroshi Hakurankai
Notes: Sprawling kitsch museum/junkyard of oddities. Check it's open before going.

Name: Pokémon × Kōgei (at Tohoku History Museum)
Notes: Pokémon x traditional crafts exhibition — final Japan venue, 10 Oct – 27 Dec 2026.

Name: Nagashima Spa Land
Notes: Roller-coaster theme park plus the huge Yuami-no-Shima onsen.

Name: X-Gold Club Nagoya Johoku
Notes: Couldn't verify the exact venue — drag the pin to the right spot.

Name: TOHO Cinemas Nagoya Sakae
Notes: 10-screen cinema in The Landmark Nagoya Sakae, 5F (opened June 2026).

Name: Hikaru Museum
Notes: Art museum with Egyptian-style architecture and Japanese & Western works.

Name: Tokugawa Art Museum
Notes: Owari Tokugawa treasures incl. Tale of Genji scrolls; Tokugawa-en garden next door.

Name: Nagoya Touken World (Samurai Museum)
Notes: Swords, armour and samurai history near Nagoya Station.

Name: Fukusaki Yokai (Tsujikawayama Park)
Notes: Hometown of yokai scholar Kunio Yanagita; the kappa that rises from the pond, yokai benches around town.

Name: Tohoku History Museum
Notes: History of the Tohoku region from prehistory onward.

Name: Naoshima (Art Island)
Notes: Chichu Art Museum, Benesse House, Art House Project, Kusama's pumpkins.

Name: National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo (MOMAT)
Notes: Japan's leading modern art collection, by the Imperial Palace moat.

Name: Meguro Parasitological Museum
Notes: Free museum of parasites incl. an 8.8 m tapeworm.

Name: Nagoya City Art Museum
Notes: Kisho Kurokawa building in Shirakawa Park (with the Science Museum).

Name: Matsuzakaya Art Museum
Notes: Exhibition space in Matsuzakaya Nagoya department store.

Name: TODAYS GALLERY STUDIO. NAGOYA
Notes: Pop-up exhibition gallery (1-17-12 Shinsakae). Check what's showing.

Name: Injuma Art House Project (a-art house)
Notes: Couldn't verify the exact venue — drag the pin to the right spot.

Name: Meiho Ski Resort
Notes: Ski resort in Gujo (winter).

Name: Takayama Old Town
Notes: Edo-era merchant streets (Sanmachi), morning markets, Hida beef.

Name: Higashiyama Zoo & Botanical Gardens
Notes: Big zoo (Shabani the gorilla) and botanical gardens.

Name: Showa-Shinzan Bear Ranch
Notes: Brown bear park beside the Showa-Shinzan lava dome near Lake Toya.

Name: Grano Grano (APITA Chiyodabashi)
Notes: In-store bakery inside APITA Chiyodabashi.

Name: Sushiro Nagoya Shinsakae
Notes: Conveyor-belt sushi.
